A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FaIRMaker framework. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable matching despite pagination and table-number changes.

before.justification: V2 reports original bias-mitigation and utility experiments, component ablations, timing measurements and DPO integration results in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds log-probability diagnostics, Fairwords diversity measurements and human–LLM judgment agreement results.

M1.justification: The optimization, filtering, refiner training and inference procedures remain the same. V3 specifies repeated scoring and a filtering margin, but these newly disclosed details do not establish a redesign of the existing filtering component.

E1.justification: Training sources and downstream coverage remain unchanged, including GA-test, BBQ-gender, MMLU, HellaSwag, Dolly Eval, Instruct Eval and BPO Eval. The added diagnostics and human validation examine existing Fairwords and response data rather than introduce new application coverage.

E2.justification: CF-D, Desc-D, Intervention and MBIAS retain their membership in the corresponding comparisons. The DPO comparison and combination experiment also remain; new internal diagnostics do not introduce another competing method.

E3.justification: Appendix B changes the reported Fairwords lengths from 20 to 20, 30 and 40, without establishing that earlier experiments were rerun. V3 also introduces log-probability and clustering diagnostic protocols and a human validation procedure using 50 randomly selected preference pairs and four annotators. The main benchmark protocols remain otherwise unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 substantially broadens supplementary validation: Section 4.6 adds refined-versus-vanilla Fairwords log-probability comparisons and semantic/lexical diversity analysis, while Appendix D.6 adds human validation of LLM judges. These address transfer behavior, Fairwords redundancy and evaluation reliability beyond the retained component ablations and case studies.

E5.justification: V3 newly discloses three evaluations per response during filtering and reports standard deviations for log-probability gaps and pairwise similarity. Both versions retain averaging over four random seeds; there is no documented increase in that run count or new confidence-interval/significance-testing practice.

E6.justification: V3 adds diagnostic results and human–LLM agreement accuracies of 86%, 90% and 84% for Dfair, GA-test and Dolly Eval, respectively. Table 6 changes FaIRMaker's win rate from 53.15% to 54.23% and sDIS from 0.224 to 0.024, reversing its sDIS ranking against w/o auto-search. These unexplained edits disagree with the retained corresponding values in Figure 3 and Table 2; they are not established performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 4.6 introduces the diagnostic definition Δp = p_chosen − p_rejected for the new log-probability-gap analysis. The optimization and refiner losses, Appendix A derivation, Algorithm 1 and BBQ metric definitions remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about automated gender-bias mitigation, utility preservation and compatibility with open- and closed-source models. Removing a repeated introductory baseline-superiority sentence does not change the comparative claims retained in the results discussion.

C2.justification: V3 adds a hypothesis that natural-language rewriting preserves Fairwords' behavioral intent and interprets the new diversity and human-agreement analyses as supporting generalizability and judge reliability. The existing emotional-cue interpretation and Appendix E limitations on bias scope and scalability remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-access link, explicitly identifies the 93-item Fairwords Bag, and specifies three scoring passes and a greater-than-0.5 filtering margin. It also identifies the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedding model and revises the documented search lengths. Existing LoRA, optimizer, hardware and training-time details are retained.

R1.justification: Six references are added, supporting evaluator selection, interpretation of adversarial token strings, semantic prompt transformation and silhouette analysis. The existing references and broad positioning remain; these additions provide targeted methodological context rather than a substantially different relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: V3 locally rewrites the refinement motivation and interpretation discussion, subdivides the ablation discussion, and adds a human-evaluation subsection and acknowledgements. The overall section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 7, 8 and 14 for the new analyses, renumbers subsequent existing tables, and expands Figure 3's caption to identify evaluators. Existing figures and prompt panels are retained with limited labeling and placement changes; the visual presentation is not comprehensively redesigned.

improvement.justification: The added diagnostics, human validation and implementation disclosures improve the paper's inspectability. However, the unexplained Table 6 edits introduce disagreements with Figure 3 and Table 2, including a reversal of whether auto-search helps on sDIS. Because v3 does not explain which values or settings apply, these reporting problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment despite the useful additions.
